item.title: Academic Search and Learning with GenAI: New Agency, New Behavior, and New Ecology
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites research exploring how generative AI is transforming academic search and learning practices. The collection seeks to examine shifts in how researchers and students interact with information systems, the emerging behaviors enabled by AI-assisted searching, and the broader changes to the information landscape that these technologies introduce.

Appel publié par Information Processing & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Academic search
  • Learning with generative AI
  • User agency
  • User behavior
  • Information ecosystems

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Foundation-model Integrity and Ranking Methods in the LLM Era
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses the challenges and opportunities surrounding the integrity of foundation models and the development of ranking methodologies in the era of large language models. The call seeks research that examines how foundation models maintain reliability and trustworthiness, as well as novel approaches to ranking and evaluating such models in information processing and management contexts.

item.title: Human Reasoning and Large Language Models: Alignments and Divergences
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the relationship between human reasoning processes and the reasoning capabilities of large language models, focusing on where their approaches align and where they diverge. The collection invites research exploring both the similarities and differences in how humans and language models understand, process, and generate information.

item.title: Explainable AI and Network Science for Social Systems and Collective Intelligence
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites contributions that explore the intersection of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) and network science as applied to social systems and collective intelligence. The call seeks research that leverages both XAI methodologies and network science approaches to better understand, model, and explain complex social phenomena, emergent behaviors, and collective decision-making processes.

Appel publié par Information Processing & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of explainable AI in understanding social systems
  • Network science approaches to modeling collective intelligence
  • Integration of XAI and network methods for social analysis
  • Interpretability in multi-agent systems and social networks
  • Transparency and accountability in AI-driven social platforms
  • Graph-based methods for explaining collective behavior
  • Knowledge graphs and social network analysis
  • Fairness and bias detection in social AI systems

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline
